symptom: On macOS, `mxcli new` for an 11.14+ (Java 25) project hung 10+ minutes in its final build step, running mxbuild with `--java-home=/usr --java-exe-path=/usr/bin/java`, Gradle at 100% CPU. `docker build`, `run --local` and `test --local` resolve the JDK the same way
cause: `resolveMacOSJavaHome` hard-coded `/usr/libexec/java_home -v 21`, so for a Java 25 project its answer always failed the major check and resolution fell through to `LookPath("java")`. On macOS /usr/bin/java is a launcher stub, not a symlink: EvalSymlinks leaves it, the derived home is /usr, and `isJDK("/usr", 25)` passes because the stub forwards `-version` to the default JDK
insight: A version probe through a forwarding launcher validates the launcher's target, not the path you derived from it — `isJDK` answered a question about a different directory than the one returned. The machine that exhibits this is one CI never runs, so the fix had to make the OS, java_home, LookPath and isJDK injectable; the fake models the stub's worst case (isJDK('/usr', n) true for every n). Revert proof: java_home -v 21 plus no /usr rejection returns /usr for a Java 25 project. Off macOS /usr is left alone — a Linux PATH java resolves through symlinks to /usr/lib/jvm/...
